subject: mathematics
question_text: If A is the matrix with rows (1, 2, 3) and (3, 2, 1), and B is the matrix with rows (3, 2, 1) and (1, 2, 3), then find 3B − 2A.

recall_prompt: Say how you would work out 3B − 2A.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Multiply by the scalars
steps.margin_note: First mark. A number times a matrix multiplies EVERY entry. Do both scalar multiplications before subtracting anything.
steps.memory_tip: A number times a matrix multiplies EVERY entry. Do both scalar multiplications before subtracting.

recall.must_convey: That 3B multiplies every entry of B by 3 and 2A multiplies every entry of A by 2, done before the subtraction.
accept: multiply every entry of B by three and every entry of A by two first
do the scalar multiplications, three times B and two times A
three B means each entry times three and two A means each entry times two
B lo prathi entry ni three tho, A lo prathi entry ni two tho multiply cheyyali
scalar multiply both matrices before subtracting
reject: find three B and two A

steps.why: Scalar multiplication reaches every entry, unlike matrix multiplication. Doing both scalars first keeps the subtraction to one clean step.
common_mistakes: Multiplying only the first row by the scalar.
Subtracting first and scaling afterwards, which changes the answer.

steps.label: Subtract entry by entry
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Subtract matching positions. Both matrices are 2×3, so the answer is 2×3 too.
steps.memory_tip: Subtract matching positions. Both are 2×3, so the answer is 2×3 too.

recall.must_convey: That the two matrices are subtracted entry by entry, giving rows (7, 2, −3) and (−3, 2, 7).
accept: subtract entry by entry to get seven two minus three and minus three two seven
take away the matching entries and the answer is a two by three matrix
corresponding entries subtract cheste answer vasthundi
the result has rows seven two minus three and minus three two seven

steps.why: Matrices add and subtract entry by entry, and only when they are the same size. Here both are 2×3, so the operation is defined.
common_mistakes: Computing 2A − 3B and getting every sign wrong.
Writing the answer as a 3×2 matrix.

insider_note: Scale each matrix before subtracting, and keep the order written: 3B − 2A, not 2A − 3B. Every entry would flip sign the other way round.
